title: Live model compatibility record
description: The cached result of the one separately authorised, potentially BILLABLE canary: that this provider and model, reached through this runtime, emitted a correctly shaped call to a tool with this contract. ⚠️ THE INVALIDATION SET IS A NESTED OBJECT RATHER THAN A CONVENTION. Everything that determines validity lives in `key` and nothing else does, so comparison is a deep equality over one object and a field added elsewhere CANNOT accidentally become a determinant — or, worse, fail to become one. A flat record would make the boundary a matter of remembering which fields to compare, and the cost of getting that wrong is either charging the operator for a check that was still valid or reusing a proof that no longer holds. ⚠️ NO TIMESTAMP, PATH, SESSION ID OR CONSENT STATE APPEARS IN `key`. Each would either invalidate the cache on every run or tie it to something that cannot change the model's behaviour. `result` carries the provenance a human needs and is deliberately outside the comparison.

key.description: The eight determinants. ⚠️ ALL REQUIRED, so a partial key cannot compare equal to a complete one — an absent field would otherwise silently mean 'matches anything'.

provider.description: Determinant 1. A different provider is a different endpoint, a different authentication path and a different wire format.

model.description: Determinant 2. Tool-calling ability is per model, and the exact id is what the project committed — never a mutable alias.

thinkingLevel.description: Determinant 3. It changes the request, and some providers reject `reasoning_effort` outright — which is a compatibility failure, not a quality difference. Retained deliberately even though it will sometimes trigger a recheck on a change that turns out to be benign: the alternative is reusing a proof taken under a request shape the provider no longer accepts.

piVersion.description: Determinant 4. The runtime builds the request and parses the tool call. Between 0.80.6 and 0.84.4 the CLI entry point, the tool `execute` signature and the discovery surface all moved; a proof taken on one is not a proof about another.

apiType.description: Determinant 5. `openai-completions` and `anthropic-messages` serialise tool calls differently, so the same model behind a different API type is an unproven path.

endpointIdentity.description: Determinant 6, STRUCTURED RATHER THAN A STRING, because a regex over a URL could exclude userinfo and a query and still accept three non-canonical spellings of one endpoint — an uppercase hostname, an implicit port and a trailing slash all validated against the previous pattern, so two records for the same endpoint would have compared unequal and re-run a billable check. The parts are produced by `canonicalizeEndpoint()` and there is exactly one of it. ⚠️ USERINFO, QUERY AND FRAGMENT ARE REFUSED BY THE CANONICALISER, not stripped: a query can carry routing, so removing it would let two differently routed endpoints share one proof, and an identity that is only non-secret after sanitising is not a property a persisted file may rely on.

scheme.description: Lowercased. `HTTPS` and `https` are one scheme and must not be two cache keys.

hostname.description: Lowercased; an IPv6 literal keeps its brackets. ⚠️ THE PATTERN REFUSES ANY UPPERCASE rather than trusting the writer to have lowered it — hostnames are case-insensitive, so an uppercase spelling is the same host and a different key.

port.description: ALWAYS EXPLICIT, with the scheme default filled in. ⚠️ `https://h/v1` and `https://h:443/v1` are the same endpoint; leaving the port implicit would make them different records.

pathname.description: PRESERVED, because a path is routing and two deployments differing only after the host are two endpoints. Canonical form: a leading slash, no trailing slash except at the root, and no empty segments.

endpointIdentitySource.description: Part of determinant 6, not a ninth. `derived` means the identity was normalised from a base URL carrying no userinfo and no query; `declared` means a human asserted a non-secret identity for an endpoint whose URL could not be used. ⚠️ IN THE KEY BECAUSE THEY ARE DIFFERENT CLAIMS ABOUT THE SAME STRING — one measured, one asserted — and a proof cached under a measured identity should not be satisfied by a run relying on an asserted one.

effectiveRequestProfile.description: Determinant 7, DERIVED FROM THE RESOLVED MODEL and recursively bounded. ⚠️ THE PREVIOUS SHAPE WAS AN OPEN OBJECT GUARDED BY PROPERTY NAME, WHICH GUARDED ALMOST NOTHING: `propertyNames` constrains only immediate keys, so `{ compat: { authorization: "Bearer …" } }` validated, and no name rule can catch a secret stored under an innocuous key like `{ innocent: "sk-live-…" }`. The projection is now closed at every level and holds scalars only. ⚠️ `Model.headers` AND `samplingParams` ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT: both are `Record<string, …>` on Pi's model, headers is where an authorization header would live, and neither changes tool-call compatibility. ⚠️ UNKNOWN FIELDS FAIL CLOSED. A compat key this schema does not name makes the record invalid, and `projectRequestProfile()` refuses to build one — so a Pi upgrade that adds a field causes a cache miss and a schema update rather than arbitrary content entering persisted state.

reasoning.description: Whether the resolved model reasons at all — it changes the request Pi sends.

resolvedThinkingValue.description: The result of applying the selected thinking level to the model's `thinkingLevelMap` — the value actually sent, not the level asked for. ⚠️ `null` IS MEANINGFUL: the map marks a level UNSUPPORTED with null, which is a different request from a level that maps to a value.

compat.description: The effective compatibility flags, scalars only. ⚠️ THE FIELD SET IS CHECKED AGAINST THE PINNED PACKAGE'S OWN TYPE DECLARATIONS BY A TEST, so this list cannot quietly fall behind Pi — the same move that stopped the trace-field guard being a hand-maintained list beside a declaration that already existed.

compatStructured.description: The compat members that are STRUCTURES rather than scalars, persisted BY VALUE because they are safely typed by Pi and can change the request. ⚠️ THEY REPLACED A DIGEST OVER THE WHOLE COMPAT OBJECT, and the digest was the defect: it hashed operator-authored open records, so a credential nested under an innocuous key became a persisted credential-derived fingerprint — exactly what REQ-0024 and section 3.12 forbid, and exactly what this file's own `digest` definition warns about. Hashing unbounded content hides it; it does not sanitise it. Only fields whose shape Pi declares are carried by value; the unbounded ones are handled by `unboundedInputs` instead.

openRouterRouting.description: Routing preferences — they select which backend serves the request, so they are determinants.

unboundedInputs.description: Request inputs whose CONTENT Kiln may neither persist nor hash. ⚠️ THEY STILL CHANGE THE REQUEST, so ignoring them would let a cached proof outlive the request it was taken against — Pi documents that `samplingParams` override named request fields, and a custom header can select a different backend. But their values are operator-authored and unbounded, so they cannot go in the file and cannot be digested either. ⚠️ THE RESOLUTION IS A DECLARED IDENTITY OR NO CACHE: when any category is present, an explicitly supplied non-secret label is required, and it is NEVER derived from the values it stands for. Without one, the canary result is not persisted and re-runs — which is the honest cost of configuration Kiln cannot inspect safely.

categories.description: Which unbounded inputs were present. ⚠️ THE CATEGORY NAMES ONLY — never a key, a value or a count, because a key name from an operator-authored record is itself unbounded content. ⚠️ AUTHENTICATION HEADERS ARE NOT A CATEGORY: they are credential transport, they are excluded from the profile entirely, and they must not invalidate a proof — rotating a key does not change what the model can do.

declaredIdentity.description: An operator-supplied, non-secret label standing for the unbounded configuration — for example a template revision or a routing profile name. ⚠️ SUPPLIED, NEVER DERIVED. Deriving it from the values would reintroduce the fingerprint this whole field exists to avoid, whatever function did the deriving.

allOf.$comment: A declared identity is required exactly when an unbounded category is present — otherwise the record would claim a proof for a request shape nothing in the key describes.

preflightContractDigest.description: Determinant 8. A digest of the EXACT canary protocol as passed to Pi: the tool name, description, input schema, the normalised prompt template, and the success predicate with its version. ⚠️ THE RANDOM CHALLENGE IS REPLACED BY A PLACEHOLDER BEFORE HASHING, or the digest would differ on every run and the cache would never hit. ⚠️ IT IS THE CONTRACT, NOT THE PACKAGE. Keying on the whole Kiln capability signature would charge the operator for a new billable check every time an unrelated planning tool changed — while the canary runs with only this tool exposed, so its proof was never about the rest of the package. Computed from the effective contract handed to Pi, so a change in how Kiln PRESENTS the tool is caught even when the schema itself is untouched.

result.description: What happened, for a human reading the file. ⚠️ DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE `key`: none of it can change whether the proof holds, and putting the timestamp in the comparison would invalidate the cache on every run.

outcome.description: ⚠️ ONLY SUCCESS IS PERSISTED. A failed canary mutates nothing and records no result (section 3.12); a stored failure would be a cache of a refusal, and the next run must retry rather than inherit it.

challengeEchoed.description: That the tool call carried the exact random challenge. The challenge VALUE is not stored — it is single-use, and keeping it would turn a liveness proof into a replayable one.
